text: Valid from 1 March 2026. This policy explains how Thornmere District Council collects household waste and recycling from the 41,300 homes in the district. It replaces the collection policy of 2023 and applies to every household that pays council tax to Thornmere, including flats above shops. The service is run by the Environmental Services team, which is led by the Head of Environmental Services, Ruth Abernathy-Coles.

Each house receives four containers. The grey bin (180 litres) is for general waste and is emptied every two weeks. The blue bin (240 litres) is for mixed dry recycling such as paper, card, food tins, drinks cans and plastic bottles, and is emptied every two weeks on the alternate week to the grey bin. The brown caddy (23 litres) is for food waste and is emptied every week. The green bin (240 litres) is for garden waste and is only provided to households that subscribe to the garden waste service. Blocks of flats with eight or more homes share larger communal bins of 1,100 litres instead, which are emptied on the same schedule.

Containers must be at the kerbside by 06:30 on the collection day and should be taken back in by 20:00 the same day. Crews work between 06:30 and 16:00, so a bin may be emptied at any time in that window. Lids must be fully closed. Crews will not empty a bin that weighs more than 60 kilograms, and they will not take extra bags placed on top of or beside a bin, because of the risk of injury and spillage. The only exceptions are household batteries and small electrical items set out as described in the Waste Services FAQ, and extra recycling during the Christmas period.

Households of six or more people can apply for a larger grey bin of 240 litres. The application form is WR-14 and must include proof of the number of residents, such as a council tax letter. Decisions on larger bins are made within 10 working days. Households that produce medical waste at home, for example from home dialysis, can receive an extra weekly collection free of charge. This collection is arranged through the Clinical Waste Officer, Daniel Ferreira-Hughes.

The garden waste service costs £52 per bin for the 2026–27 season, which runs from 1 April 2026 to 31 March 2027. Residents who hold a Thornmere Council Tax Reduction award pay a reduced price of £26 per bin. A household may subscribe for up to three green bins. Garden waste is collected every two weeks from March to November, and once a month in December, January and February. The price is the same whenever in the season a subscription is bought, so subscriptions bought after 31 May are not reduced.

Bulky items such as sofas, beds, wardrobes and fridges are collected for a fee. The standard charge is £35.00 for up to three items and £8.50 for each further item, with a maximum of eight items per booking. Residents who receive Council Tax Reduction pay half of the standard charge. Bookings must be made at least five working days before the collection date. Each booking has a reference number starting with the letters BW, and this reference must be written on a label attached to every item.

Bulky items must be left outside by 07:00 on the collection day, in a place the crew can reach without entering a building. Mattresses must be wrapped in plastic. The Council does not collect building rubble, car parts, tyres, gas bottles or asbestos as bulky waste.

If a bin has not been emptied, residents should report it within two working days of the scheduled collection day. Reports made after that are not accepted, and the bin will be emptied on the next normal collection day. The Council aims to return for a reported missed bin within three working days. If the crew recorded that the bin was not out by 06:30, was contaminated or was overweight, the bin will not be collected again until the next scheduled day.

Recycling that contains the wrong items is treated as contaminated. The crew leaves a yellow tag on a contaminated blue bin and does not empty it. After a third yellow tag in any 12-month period, an Education Officer visits the household to explain the rules. Repeated contamination after that visit can lead to a fixed penalty notice of £80, which is reduced to £50 if it is paid within 14 days.

Residents who cannot move their bins because of age, disability or illness, and who have no one else in the home aged over 16 who can help, can apply for an assisted collection. With an assisted collection, the crew collects the bins from an agreed point on the property and returns them there afterwards. Assisted collections are reviewed every two years.

New and replacement bins are delivered within 15 working days of the request. A replacement grey or blue bin costs £28, except where a Council crew damaged the bin, in which case it is replaced free of charge. Bins for newly built homes are paid for by the developer at £96 per property for a full set. Bins remain the property of the Council and must stay at the address when a resident moves house.

The Council runs one Household Recycling Centre, at Sandpiper Road. It is open 08:00–18:00 from April to September and 08:00–16:00 from October to March, and it is closed on 25 and 26 December and on 1 January. Vans, and trailers longer than 2.5 metres, need a permit, and each household can receive up to 12 van permits per year. Residents must show proof of address on entry.

Questions about this policy can be sent to the Waste Services Contact Centre on 01632 960 418, which is open Monday to Friday, 08:30–17:00. Formal complaints are answered within 20 working days.

How do I find my collection day? Enter your postcode in the collection day checker on the Thornmere District Council website. The district is divided into 10 collection rounds, named Round A to Round J, and each round has a fixed weekday. Your grey and blue bins are emptied on alternate weeks, and your brown food caddy is emptied every week on the same day.

What time should my bins be out? Put your containers at the kerbside by 06:30 on your collection day. Crews work until 16:00, so please do not report a bin as missed before 16:30. Bring your bins back in by 20:00 the same day.

My bin was missed. What should I do? Report it online or by phone within two working days of your collection day. You will receive a reference number starting with MC, and we aim to return within three working days. If you report it later than two working days, we will empty the bin on your next normal collection day instead.

Will collections change over Christmas? Yes. There will be no collections on Friday 25 December 2026 or on Friday 1 January 2027. Collections due on 25 December will take place on Sunday 27 December, and collections due on 1 January will take place on Saturday 2 January 2027. Collections on all other days during the holiday period stay on their normal day.

Can I put out extra recycling after Christmas? Yes. Between 21 December 2026 and 8 January 2027, crews will take up to two extra bags of recycling placed beside your blue bin, as long as the bags are clear so the crew can see what is inside. Outside these dates, the normal rule applies and extra bags beside any bin are not collected. Flattened cardboard boxes can also be placed beside the blue bin during this period.

What happens to my real Christmas tree? If you subscribe to the garden waste service, put your tree out next to your green bin on your garden waste day in the two weeks starting Monday 4 January 2027. Trees must be cut into pieces no longer than 1.2 metres, with all decorations, pots and stands removed. Artificial trees are not accepted. Households without a garden waste subscription can take real trees to the Household Recycling Centre at Sandpiper Road free of charge.

How do I join the garden waste service, and what does it cost? You can subscribe online or by phone. The 2026–27 season costs £52 per bin, or £26 per bin for households with a Council Tax Reduction award, and you can have up to three bins. New subscribers receive their green bin within 15 working days.

Can I get a refund if I move? Garden waste refunds are only given if you move out of the district before 30 September. In that case you receive 50% of the price you paid. Moves within the district do not qualify, because the subscription moves with you to your new address.

How do I book a bulky waste collection? Book online or by phone at least five working days in advance. The charge is £35.00 for up to three items and £8.50 for each further item, up to a maximum of eight items. You can cancel free of charge until 12:00 on the working day before the collection. After that time, the charge is not refunded.

How do I get rid of batteries and small electrical items? Put household batteries in a clear sealed bag on top of your blue bin lid. Small electrical items that are no bigger than a shoebox, such as kettles and phone chargers, can be placed in a carrier bag next to your blue bin. Larger electrical items must be booked as bulky waste or taken to Sandpiper Road.

Do you collect glass? No, glass is not collected from the kerbside. Please use one of the 64 bottle banks across the district or take glass to Sandpiper Road.

What can go in my food caddy? All cooked and uncooked food, including meat, fish, bones, tea bags and coffee grounds, can go in the brown caddy. Use only compostable liners, never plastic bags. Each household can collect one free roll of 52 compostable liners per year from any district library, and further rolls cost £3.50 each.

What if my bin is damaged or stolen? Report it online or by phone. A replacement grey or blue bin costs £28 and is delivered within 15 working days. If the damage was caused by one of our crews, the replacement is free. A replacement food caddy is always free of charge.

How do I apply for an assisted collection? Complete form WR-22 online or ask the contact centre to send you a paper copy. An officer may visit to agree a collection point, and a decision is made within 15 working days.

How do I contact Waste Services? Call the Waste Services Contact Centre on 01632 960 418, Monday to Friday, 08:30–17:00. To report dangerous dumped waste, such as needles or chemicals, outside these hours, call 01632 960 999.

Welcome to Dunmarra Language Centre. The Centre teaches English, Spanish, German and Japanese to adults and to young people aged 16 and over. Teaching is organised by the Director of Studies, Ines Moreau-Batista, and all questions about enrolment, fees, accommodation and certificates are handled by the Student Services Manager, Kofi Adjei-Brandt. The office is open Monday to Friday, 08:30–17:30.

Before your course starts you must take the online placement test. The test takes about 45 minutes and must be completed at least three days before your first lesson. If you have not taken it by then, you will take a paper test at 08:30 on your first Monday and start lessons one day later. There are six levels, from Level 1 (beginner) to Level 6 (advanced).

The Standard course has 15 hours of lessons per week. Classes run Monday to Friday from 09:15 to 12:30, with a break from 10:45 to 11:00. The Intensive course has 25 hours per week and adds afternoon workshops from 13:30 to 15:30, Monday to Friday. The Evening course has 4 hours per week, on Tuesday and Thursday from 18:30 to 20:30, and is sold in blocks of four weeks. New Standard and Intensive students can start on any Monday, while Evening blocks start on fixed dates.

Standard and Evening classes have a maximum of 12 students, and the afternoon workshops of the Intensive course have a maximum of 8 students. A class needs at least 4 students to run. If fewer than 4 students are booked for a level, the class runs as a mini-group with two thirds of the normal lesson hours, and the price does not change.

The Standard course costs €265 per week, the Intensive course costs €395 per week, and the Evening course costs €180 per four-week block. Every new student pays a registration fee of €60 once, and course books cost €38 per level. Students who book 12 weeks or more receive a 10% discount on tuition, and students who book 24 weeks or more receive a 15% discount. The discounts do not apply to Evening courses, the registration fee, books or accommodation.

The full course fee must be paid at least 14 days before the course starts. Students on courses of 24 weeks or more may pay in instalments instead, as explained in the fees guide. Payments by bank transfer must show your student number with the prefix DLC, for example DLC-40217, so that the payment can be matched to your account. Students who book late, less than 14 days before the start, must pay in full at the time of booking.

Regular attendance is required. You must attend at least 80% of your lessons to receive a course certificate. Students who hold a student visa must attend at least 85% of their lessons, and the Centre must report lower attendance to the immigration authorities. If you will be absent, please tell the office by 09:00 on the day. Students who arrive more than 15 minutes late are marked absent for the first lesson of the day.

The Centre is closed on public holidays, and lessons that fall on a public holiday are not made up or refunded. The Centre is also closed for the winter break from 21 December 2026 to 3 January 2027. Weeks during the winter break are not counted as part of your course, so the end date of a course that includes the break moves back by two weeks.

You can change from one course type to another with one week's notice, as long as there is space. Changes of level after your first week need the agreement of your teacher and the Director of Studies. Certificates are given out in class on the last Friday of your course, and a replacement certificate costs €15.

The Centre is an official test venue for the Dunmarra Proficiency Test (DPT). Registration for each DPT session closes six weeks before the exam date, and the exam fee is €145. Students who want to take the DPT should speak to their teacher about the right level before registering.

The Centre can arrange a room with a host family. Host family accommodation costs €210 per week for a single room with breakfast and evening meal, plus a one-off placement fee of €45. Requests must reach the office at least four weeks before arrival. All host families are within 40 minutes of the Centre by public transport.

Students aged 16 or 17 can join Standard and Intensive courses only. They must bring the parental consent form U18, signed by a parent or guardian, on their first day, and they must stay with a host family arranged by the Centre. Students under 18 may not leave their host family after 22:00 unless an adult from the family is with them.

The study centre on the second floor is open 08:00–19:00 from Monday to Friday and can be used by all students free of charge. A free conversation club takes place every Wednesday from 15:45 to 17:00. The social programme includes a guided excursion every Saturday, which costs between €25 and €40 depending on the destination and must be booked at reception by 12:00 on the Thursday before.

Students who hold a student visa must have health insurance for the full length of their course. The Centre can arrange insurance for €12 per week. Students must show proof of their own insurance, or buy the Centre's insurance, before their first lesson.

If you are unhappy with any part of your course, please speak first to your teacher. If the problem is not solved, write to the Student Services Manager at studentservices@dunmarra-lc.example. You will receive a written answer within 7 working days.

What do I pay when I book? You pay a registration fee of €60, the tuition for your course, and €38 for each course book you need. The registration fee is paid once, even if you book further courses later, and it is never refunded. If you book accommodation, you also pay the host family placement fee of €45.

How much is tuition? The Standard course (15 hours per week) costs €265 per week and the Intensive course (25 hours per week) costs €395 per week. Evening courses cost €180 per four-week block. If you book 12 weeks or more of Standard or Intensive lessons in one booking, you receive 10% off tuition, and for 24 weeks or more you receive 15% off. Two shorter bookings cannot be added together to reach a discount level.

When do I have to pay? Full payment is due at least 14 days before your course starts. For courses of 24 weeks or more, you can choose to pay in three instalments instead: 40% when you book, 30% before the start of week 8 and 30% before the start of week 16. If an instalment is more than 7 days late, your place may be suspended until it is paid.

How can I pay? You can pay by bank transfer or by card. Card payments of more than €1,000 carry a surcharge of 1.5%. Please always include your student number with the prefix DLC as the payment reference. We do not accept cash at the office.

What is included in the tuition fee? Tuition includes the placement test, all lessons, the course certificate, use of the study centre and Wi-Fi in the building. Course books, exam fees, excursions and accommodation are not included.

Can I change my course after I have booked? Before your course starts, you can change the course type or the start date free of charge. After the start, you can change course type with one week's notice if there is space. If the new course costs more, you pay the difference; if it costs less, the difference is given as a credit note. The first change after the start is free, and each further change costs €20.

What if I cancel before my course starts? If you cancel 28 days or more before the start date, we refund all tuition fees. If you cancel between 7 and 27 days before the start date, we refund 50% of tuition fees. If you cancel less than 7 days before the start date, no tuition is refunded. In every case the registration fee of €60 is kept, and books that have already been given to you are not refunded.

What if my visa is refused? If your student visa application is refused, we refund all fees you have paid except an administration charge of €150. To receive this refund, you must send us a copy of the refusal letter within 10 days of the date of the decision. This rule applies even if the course starts within 7 days.

Can I get money back if I leave my course early? We do not give cash refunds once a course has started. Instead, if you leave early, you receive a credit note for the unused full weeks of tuition. The credit note can be used for any course at the Centre and is valid for 12 months from the date it is issued.

Can I take a holiday during my course? Students on courses of 12 weeks or more can take one week of holiday for every 12 weeks booked. You must tell the office at least two weeks before the holiday. Your course end date moves back by the number of holiday weeks, and you do not pay extra for these weeks.

How much does the Dunmarra Proficiency Test cost? The DPT costs €145. The next two sessions are on Saturday 21 November 2026 and Saturday 6 March 2027, and registration closes six weeks before each date. Exam fees are only refunded if you are ill on the exam day and send a medical certificate within 5 working days, and the refund is 75% of the fee.

What does host family accommodation cost? A single room with breakfast and evening meal costs €210 per week, plus the €45 placement fee. If you cancel your host family less than 7 days before you arrive, you pay for one week. Extra nights before or after your booking cost €34 per night, if the family can offer them.

Do you offer airport transfers? Yes. A transfer from Dunmarra Airport to your accommodation costs €70 one way, and it must be booked at least 5 days before you arrive. If your flight is delayed, the driver waits for up to 90 minutes at no extra cost.

What if I lose my student card? A replacement student card costs €10 and is ready the next working day. You need your student card to enter the building after 17:30.

Gullstone Harbour Marina is owned and run by the Gullstone Harbour Trust. The marina has 420 berths on eight pontoons, labelled A to H. These regulations apply to everyone who holds an annual berth licence, and to their crew and guests. The Marina Manager is Siobhan Achterberg, and the Harbour Master is Captain Rafael Okoro-Lunn, who is responsible for safety and navigation within the harbour limits.

An annual berth licence runs from 1 April to 31 March. Licence fees are charged per metre of the vessel's overall length, including bowsprits, davits and outboard brackets. The fee for the 2026–27 licence year is €395 per metre on pontoons A to E and €350 per metre on pontoons F to H, including VAT. The minimum charge is for a length of 8 metres, so a 6.5-metre boat pays the same as an 8-metre boat.

The full fee is due by 1 April. Berth holders may instead pay by 10 monthly direct debits from April to January, with a surcharge of 4% on the total fee. Existing berth holders must confirm that they want to renew their licence by 15 February. Berths that have not been renewed by that date may be offered to the next person on the waiting list.

Anyone may join the waiting list by paying a deposit of €250. The deposit is taken off the first licence fee when a berth is offered, or returned in full if the person leaves the list. Berths are offered in order of the date of joining, but a berth can only be offered if it suits the length, beam and draught of the vessel.

Every vessel must have third-party liability insurance of at least €3,000,000. Berth holders must send a copy of their insurance certificate to the marina office each year before 1 April, and a vessel without valid insurance may be refused entry or moved. The vessel must also be kept in a seaworthy condition and must clearly show its name.

The speed limit is 3 knots inside the marina and 5 knots in the approach channel. Skippers should call the marina office on VHF channel 80 before arrival or departure. The marina office is open 08:00–20:00 from May to September and 09:00–17:00 from October to April.

Shore power is metered at each berth and charged at €0.38 per kWh. The maximum supply is 16 amps per berth. Shore power cables must be disconnected whenever a vessel is left unattended for more than 7 days, unless a heater or dehumidifier has been approved by the office.

Berth holders may sleep on board for up to 3 nights in any week without permission. Living on board for longer requires a liveaboard permit, which costs €600 per year, and no more than 15 liveaboard permits are issued at any time. Sub-letting a berth is not allowed. Berths may only be swapped through the marina office.

Berth holders should tell the office when their vessel will be away from its berth for more than 48 hours, so that the berth can be used for visitors. Berth holders who report an absence of 7 nights or more receive a credit of 20% of the visitor fees earned on their berth, up to €300 per licence year. The credit is applied to the next licence invoice.

The fuel pontoon is open 08:30–18:00 every day from April to October. Engines must be switched off while fuelling, and smoking is not allowed anywhere on the fuel pontoon. Oily waste and used engine oil must be taken to the collection point next to the boatyard. The black water pump-out at the end of pontoon D is free for berth holders.

Hot work, such as welding, grinding or the use of open flames, is not allowed on the pontoons without a Hot Work Permit (form HW-3) from the Harbour Master, which must be requested at least 24 hours in advance. Antifouling and hull scraping may only be done in the boatyard. A lift-out costs €14 per metre, and storage on the hard costs €6.50 per metre per week.

Each berth licence includes one permit for the berth holders' car park, and further permits cost €45 per year. Berth holders may bring up to 6 guests onto the pontoons at any one time, and guests must be accompanied by the berth holder or a named crew member. Children under 12 must wear a lifejacket on the pontoons.

Between 1 November and 28 February, berth holders must check their mooring lines and fenders at least once every 14 days, or name a keyholder who will do this for them. The marina offers a boat-check service for €35 per month, which includes a weekly visual check and a written report after any storm warning.

Dogs are welcome but must be kept on a lead on the pontoons and in the car park. The code for the pontoon gates changes on the first day of each month and is sent to berth holders by text message.

The Trust may end a licence with 28 days' written notice if the berth holder seriously or repeatedly breaks these regulations. A berth holder may end the licence by giving 3 months' written notice. In that case the unused part of the fee is refunded pro rata, minus an administration charge of €150.

Last updated: 18 June 2026. This page answers common questions from visiting skippers. Visitors are welcome all year round, and visitor berths are managed by the same marina office as the annual berths.

Where will I be berthed? Most visitors are berthed on pontoon V, which has 40 visitor berths. When pontoon V is full, visitors may be placed on resident berths that are free while their owners are away. The marina can take vessels up to 24 metres in overall length and up to 3.2 metres draught at the lowest tide.

Can I book in advance? Yes. Visitor berths can be booked up to 60 days ahead through the online booking page or by phone. Without a booking, call the marina office on VHF channel 80 when you approach the harbour. The office is open 08:00–20:00 from May to September and 09:00–17:00 from October to April.

How much does a visitor berth cost? From May to September the price is €4.20 per metre per night, and from October to April it is €2.90 per metre per night. Every vessel is charged for at least 8 metres. Multihulls pay 50% more than the normal price. If you stay 7 nights in a row, you pay for only 6.

Can I stop for a few hours only? Yes. A short stay of up to 4 hours between 10:00 and 16:00 costs a flat fee of €12, whatever the size of the vessel. If you stay past 16:00, you are charged the full nightly rate instead.

What is included in the price? Showers and toilets are included, and the access code is given to you when you register. Wi-Fi is free on the network called GHM-Visitor. Electricity is not included and costs a flat €5 per night. The laundry costs €6 per wash and €4 per dry.

What if I arrive when the office is closed? Use the night berth at the end of pontoon V and register at the office by 09:30 the next morning. If the night berth is taken, raft up alongside another visitor and leave fenders out on both sides.

When do I have to leave? Departure time is 12:00 noon. If you leave after 14:00, you are charged for another night. Please return your key card to the office when you leave, because a lost key card costs €20.

Can I cancel a booking? Bookings cancelled more than 72 hours before the arrival date are free of charge. If you cancel later, or do not arrive, you are charged for one night.

Are there discounts for groups? Groups of 6 or more boats that book together receive 10% off visitor berth fees. Cruising clubs and rallies should contact the Events Coordinator, Mateus Sandoval-Obi, at least 4 weeks before arrival.

Can I get fuel and use the pump-out? The fuel pontoon is open 08:30–18:00 every day from April to October. The black water pump-out at the end of pontoon D costs €15 per use for visitors.

Are there any restrictions on entering the harbour? Vessels with a draught of more than 2.5 metres should not enter or leave within 2 hours either side of low water. The speed limit is 3 knots inside the marina. When winds of force 7 or more are forecast, the office may ask visitors on the outer end of pontoon V to move to the inner pontoons.

Can I leave my boat here and go home for a while? Yes. Visitors may leave their boat unattended for up to 14 nights, as long as the office has the phone number of a keyholder. Visitors who want to stay longer than 28 nights between October and April can apply for a temporary monthly berth, which costs €95 per metre per month. Temporary monthly berths are not available from May to September.

Where can I park my car? Visitors can park one car in the visitor car park for €8 per day, for up to 7 days. Car park tickets are sold at the marina office. The berth holders' car park is for permit holders only.

Is there a shop nearby? The marina chandlery next to the office is open 09:00–17:00 every day except Tuesday and sells charts, gas refills and basic food. Visitors receive 5% off chandlery purchases when they show their berth receipt.

Can I bring my dog? Yes, dogs are welcome on board and ashore. They must be kept on a lead on the pontoons and in the car park.

Bramblecot Day Nursery cares for children aged 6 months to 5 years. The nursery is registered for 62 places and is owned by Bramblecot Nurseries Ltd. The Nursery Manager is Hannah Ruiz-Petit and the Deputy Manager is Gwen Rossiter-Mbeki. One of them is always on site while the nursery is open.

Children are cared for in three rooms. The Seedlings room is for babies aged 6 months to 2 years, with one adult for every 3 children. The Saplings room is for children aged 2 to 3 years, with one adult for every 4 children. The Oaks room is for children aged 3 to 5 years, with one adult for every 8 children. Children usually move up to the next room in the month after their birthday, after a two-week transition.

The nursery is open Monday to Friday, 07:30–18:30, for 51 weeks of the year. It closes for one week between Christmas and New Year and on all public holidays. Children can attend for a full day (07:30–18:30), a morning session (07:30–13:00) or an afternoon session (13:00–18:30). The minimum booking is two sessions per week.

Every child has a key person, a named practitioner who looks after the child's care and learning and is the main contact for the family. Parents can see photos and notes in their child's online learning journal in the Bramblecot Journal app, which is updated at least once a week. Parent meetings with the key person take place twice a year, in March and October.

Before a child starts, we offer two free settling-in sessions of up to two hours each. These take place in the two weeks before the start date, and a parent or carer stays for at least the first session. When a place is accepted, parents pay a registration fee of £50, which is not refundable, and a deposit of £150. The deposit is returned with the final invoice when the child leaves.

Fees depend on the child's age and the type of session. They are set out in the yearly fee notice; for example, a full day for a child under 2 costs £68.50. Fees are invoiced monthly in advance and must be paid by the 5th of each month. A late payment fee of £25 is added if the fees have not been paid by the 15th of the month.

Children must be collected by 18:30. A late collection charge of £15 is made for each 15 minutes, or part of 15 minutes, after 18:30. If a child has not been collected by 19:00 and we have not been able to contact the parents or emergency contacts, the nursery follows its uncollected child procedure.

Children may only be collected by the adults named on the registration form, who must be aged 16 or over. If someone else needs to collect your child, please phone the nursery in advance and give that person your family password. Without the password, staff will not release the child.

Children who are unwell should not attend. A child with a temperature of 38°C or above will be sent home. After vomiting or diarrhoea, a child must stay away from nursery until 48 hours after the last episode. Parents should tell the nursery by 09:00 if their child will be absent through illness.

Staff can give prescribed medicine only if it is in its original packaging with the pharmacy label, and only after a parent has completed form MED-1. Paracetamol that has not been prescribed can be given only with written consent, after staff have phoned a parent, and on no more than 3 days in a row.

All meals and snacks are included in the fees. Breakfast is served until 08:30, lunch at 11:45 and tea at 16:00. The nursery is nut-free, and all allergies must be recorded on the registration form and confirmed by a doctor's letter. Parents provide nappies and wipes, while the nursery provides sun cream unless a child needs a special one.

Children go outside every day unless the weather is dangerous, so please send them with clothes for all weather and a full set of spare clothes, all labelled with the child's name. Babies sleep according to their routine at home. Older children have a quiet rest time from 12:30 to 14:00, but no child is woken or kept awake against the parents' wishes.

Outings to the park and the library take place with written consent from parents, which is given once on the registration form. On outings, there is one adult for every 2 children under 2 and one adult for every 4 children aged 2 and over.

The Deputy Manager, Gwen Rossiter-Mbeki, is the Designated Safeguarding Lead. Staff and visitors may not use mobile phones in any of the children's rooms, and photos of children are taken only on nursery tablets.

All accidents are recorded, and parents are asked to sign the accident form on the same day. For any bump to the head, staff phone a parent straight away.

Parents must give at least four weeks' written notice to leave the nursery or to reduce sessions. If less notice is given, four weeks' fees are charged in place of notice.

If you have a concern, please speak to your child's key person or the Nursery Manager. Written complaints receive a reply within 10 working days. If you are still unhappy, you can write to the director of Bramblecot Nurseries Ltd, Leon Castellano-Wirth.

These fees apply from 1 September 2026. They replace the fees for 2025–26 and stay in place until at least 31 August 2027. We review fees once a year and give parents at least 8 weeks' notice of any increase.

For children under 2, a full day (07:30–18:30) costs £68.50, a morning session (07:30–13:00) costs £41.00 and an afternoon session (13:00–18:30) costs £37.00. For children aged 2 and over, a full day costs £64.00, a morning session costs £38.50 and an afternoon session costs £34.50. The lower rate starts from the first day of the month after a child's second birthday.

Monthly invoices are the same each month. They are calculated by multiplying the weekly fee by 51 and dividing by 12. For example, three full days per week for a child under 2 cost £205.50 per week, which gives a monthly invoice of £873.38.

The morning session includes breakfast and lunch, and the afternoon session includes tea. All sessions include snacks, milk and drinks. There is no reduction for children who bring their own food for medical or religious reasons.

Families with two or more children at the nursery at the same time receive a sibling discount of 10%. The discount is taken off the fees of the older child. It does not apply to funded hours or to extra sessions.

Children who are eligible for funded hours can use 15 or 30 funded hours per week for 38 weeks of the year. Parents can instead choose to spread their funded hours across 51 weeks, which gives about 11.2 hours per week for a 15-hour entitlement and about 22.4 hours per week for a 30-hour entitlement. Families using funded hours pay a charge of £7.00 for each funded day to cover meals and consumables. Funded hours cannot be used for the late collection charge.

Two optional activities are charged in addition to the session fees. The music class on Wednesday mornings costs £4.50 per session, and Forest School for children in the Oaks room costs £6.00 per session on Fridays. Parents can sign up or stop at the start of each half term. Nappies and wipes are not included in the fees and must be provided by parents.

Requests to add regular sessions take effect from the 1st of the following month, if there is space. Requests to reduce sessions need at least four weeks' written notice, as for leaving the nursery. The minimum booking remains two sessions per week.

Extra sessions can be booked at least 48 hours in advance if there is space in the room. They are charged at the normal session price plus 10%. Extra sessions cancelled with less than 24 hours' notice are charged in full.

Fees are not reduced for sickness, holidays or days when the nursery is closed for public holidays. As the one exception, children who attend all year can take two weeks of holiday each year at half fees, as long as parents give at least four weeks' written notice. Unused holiday weeks do not carry over to the next year.

The nursery will be closed from Thursday 24 December 2026 to Friday 1 January 2027 and will reopen on Monday 4 January 2027. No fees are charged for the closure week, because it is not one of the 51 weeks for which the nursery is open.

Fees are invoiced monthly in advance and must be paid by the 5th of each month. A late payment fee of £25 is added to fees not paid by the 15th. If fees for two months remain unpaid, the nursery will send a written warning, and the place may be withdrawn 14 days after the warning.

You can pay by bank transfer, by childcare voucher or through a tax-free childcare account. Please always use your child's account number, which starts with BC, as the payment reference. We do not accept cash or cheques.

A registration fee of £50 and a deposit of £150 are paid when a place is accepted. The deposit is returned with the final invoice. The late collection charge is £15 for each 15 minutes, or part of 15 minutes, after 18:30.

Questions about fees should be sent to the Nursery Administrator, Pavel Nwosu-Hart, who is in the office on Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday from 09:00 to 15:00. Invoices are sent by email on the 25th of the month before they are due.
